cost_time: Registry fees modest (~USD 50-150) + notarial deed ~USD 200-500; ~15 days after a complete file; official fees unpublished; a local legal representative is required for foreigners.
notes: International ONGDs must register in the Registro Público de ONGD; moderate bureaucracy; all filings in Spanish. | verify-rest 2026-10: granting body is SGJD/DIRRSAC (not the Judiciary/Chancillería)
bottleneck: SGJD/DIRRSAC legal-personality filing plus local address/representative; all filings in Spanish.
deduction: limited: donations to registered OSCs eligible for income-tax credit (LIR); verify current cap
donor_restr: international ONGDs must register in the Registro Publico de ONGD (DIREF) and report agreements with the State
compliance: Ley Especial de Fomento ONGD (Decreto 32-2011): keep SEIP/DIREF personality records current and file annual reports to the secretariat. Inactivity, dissolution or breach: personality and registration cancelled.
tax_exempt: No separate published charitable tax-exempt application; incorporation with charitable objects gives legal personality only. Donations to charitable/educational institutions deductible up to 10% of net taxable income.
bank_access: Needs a local visit: banks require the applicant to appear with passport, residency/visa proof and an NIT (tax registration); a remote founder would need a local agent or an in-person trip.

entity: Asociación or fundación under Ley 1115 (Ley General de Regulación y Control de Organismos sin Fines de Lucro, 2022; reformed by Ley 1127/2022 and Ley 1212/2024), registered with the Ministerio de Gobernación; fideicomiso (Ley 741/2010).
requirements: Spanish articles, local address, registration with the Ministerio de Gobernación (Dirección General de Registro y Control de OSFL), which now grants and cancels legal status directly; Ley 1040/2020 (Agentes Extranjeros) applies to foreign-funded entities.
cost_time: US$300–800; 4–8 weeks if granted. Notary for the public deed adds ~US$100–300; official processing time unpublished; foreigners need no local residence.
notes: Avoid: government has dissolved 5,700+ NGO legal personalities since 2018, including foreign-funded ones; laws target foreign-financed civil society, so an Australian-founded charity faces extreme cancellation/political risk. | confirm prior 'very hard'; add Ley 1115 (2022) as the controlling OSFL regulation; mass cancellations by Ministry of Governance decrees continue | verify-rest 2026-10: Ley 1115 (2022, reformed 2022/2024) is now the controlling law; legal personality granted by Gobernación, not the National Assembly
bottleneck: Extreme political risk: 5,700+ NGO legal personalities cancelled since 2018; state controls authorization and registry of OSFLs.
deduction: deductible for NI donors to tax-exempt OSFLs (moot if operating)
donor_restr: Ley 1115 (2022) gives the government broad control, supervision and cancellation power over OSFLs; foreign-funded NGOs systematically targeted
compliance: Legal personality is granted and cancelled by the Ministerio de Gobernación (Ley 1115); entities file financial statements, donor lists and activity reports with Gobernación; non-compliance leads to cancellation.
tax_exempt: Not automatic: apply to the DGI (Ministry of Finance) proving income serves charitable purposes (LCT art. 32, 2024 reform) for ISR exemption; no general donor deduction; approval time unpublished.
bank_access: In-person visit required; non-resident foreigners need passport plus a second photo ID and typically two personal/professional references; remote opening not offered.

entity: Asociación (Ley 218 de 1939); fundación (Ley de Fundaciones No. 5338 de 1973); fideicomiso — inscription at the Registro de Personas Jurídicas (Registro Nacional).
requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Personas Jurídicas; 3+ members for an asociación; a fundación's Junta Administrativa must include one member appointed by the Executive and one by the cantonal municipality.
cost_time: US$1,000–2,500 incl. notary; 4–8 weeks for registration, tax exemption takes months. Notary fee ~US$300–600; official timelines unpublished.
notes: Stable, professional services widely available in English; donor tax exemption requires separate Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) approval. | correct prior: asociacion requires 5+ founders (Ley 218), not 3+; donor deduction needs the interes publico decree, MINFIN covers entity exemption | verify-rest 2026-10: foundations governed by Ley 5338; registry is the Registro de Personas Jurídicas (not commercial registry/Education Ministry)
bottleneck: Public deed before a CR notary + local office; asociaciones need 5+ members, so a fundacion (single founder) is the practical path.
time_to_reg: 4-8 weeks (entity); interes publico decree adds months
deduction: donor deduction requires 'interes publico' decree (Consejo de Ministros); entity tax exemption via MINFIN (separate)
donor_restr: none notable; foreign founders and members permitted; no FCRA-style regime
compliance: Since 2024, OSFL must register in the Banco Central's RTBF transparency registry (beneficial owners) and file annual financial/AML reports. Sanctions for non-compliance; statutes govern associations.
tax_exempt: Separate application: file with the Dirección General de Hacienda via Exonet (Ley 10.286/2022) for ISR exemption of income devoted to charitable aims. Donors deduct 100% (Ley 9.637). Approval usually months.
bank_access: Most banks require DIMEX residency per SUGEF KYC rules; non-residents can open only a simplified in-person account with low monthly deposit caps, unsuitable for a charity.

entity: Fundación de interés privado (Ley 25/1995; min endowment US$10,000); asociación sin fines de lucro (personería jurídica from the Ministerio de Gobierno); fideicomiso (Ley 21 of 10 May 2017, replacing Ley 1/1984).
requirements: Spanish articles and name, local registered office, board of 3+ members, IFPF registration; single foreign founder permitted, no local nationals required.
cost_time: US$2,500–4,500 incl. notary; ~US$400/yr maintenance; 4–8 weeks. Foreigners may establish a FIP (not barred); official timelines unpublished.
notes: The FIP (Ley No. 8 de 2000) is the most popular expat foundation vehicle in Latin America; IFPF is a specialized fast registry; strong English-language support. | correct prior: FIP is governed by Ley 25 de 1995 (not 'Ley 8 de 2000'); registered in Registro Publico de la Propiedad, not 'IFPF' | Verified: Personero legal extranjero debe residir en Panamá; acta protocolizada en notaría y Tasa Única B/.400 | verify-rest 2026-10: trust law is Ley 21/2017; FIP needs a Panamanian resident agent and a council of 3 natural persons or 1 legal entity
bottleneck: Panamanian registered office plus public deed before a Panama notary; registry work handled by a local firm (remote founder fine).
deduction: deductible for PA donors up to ~5% of taxable income for approved charitable entities; entity exemption via MINA (separate)
donor_restr: none notable; no residency requirement; single foreign founder and foreign board permitted
compliance: FIPs must pay the annual tasa única (~USD 300) to the Registro Público via e-Tax 2.0 each year by 15 July, keep ledgers current, and notify the registry of changes. Non-payment forfeits legal status.
tax_exempt: Non-profit income exempt under the Código Fiscal if devoted to its purpose (DGI verifies at filing). Donor deductions require a separate DGI authorization; DGI revoked such benefits in 2025; timing unpublished.
bank_access: Non-residents may open accounts in-person with passport, foreign address proof, home-bank reference and income proof; AML Law 23 KYC and an interview apply; no residency needed.

entity: Fundación, asociación or corporación (personas jurídicas sin ánimo de lucro, Código Civil arts. 633-652) — registro ante Cámara de Comercio under Decreto 2150/1995 arts. 40-45 and Decreto 427/1996.
requirements: No nationality requirement for board; Colombian registered address; constitution by private document with recognized signatures (public deed not required) registered at the Cámara de Comercio; filings in Spanish.
cost_time: US$300–600 incl. lawyer; 2–6 weeks at Cámara de Comercio. Notary for the deed ~US$50–150; official timelines unpublished.
notes: Most expat-friendly in the region; foreigners can be president/directors; Bogotá has strong English-speaking legal market; donation tax deductions require separate DIAN certification; 2023 NGO-law reforms (Ley 2287/2022) added transparency reporting for foreign-funded entities. | Prior context confirmed; deduction is a separate DIAN certification step, not automatic; Ley 2287/2022 adds transparency duties | Verified: Constitution deed must be signed before a Colombian notary; remote founders need an apostilled poder especial | verify-rest 2026-10: Civil Code articles corrected to 633-652; private document suffices for ESAL constitution
bottleneck: Colombian registered address + local lawyer for public deed & Cámara de Comercio registration; Spanish filings
deduction: Separate DIAN certification (calificación) required; donations to certified entities are deductible
donor_restr: Ley 2287/2022 NGO transparency regime: annual reporting + public disclosure of foreign contributions; no licensing
compliance: Foundations and associations renew chamber registration and file annual financials, board minutes and activity reports by ~31 March; fines apply for non-filing, prolonged inactivity risks cancellation.
tax_exempt: No separate tax step: ESALs are special-regime taxpayers (art. 19 E.T.); DIAN exempts non-distributed income where bylaws show a charitable general-interest purpose. Donors deduct up to 15% of taxable income.
bank_access: Requires cédula de extranjería (residency ID) plus local address proof; tourist status is rejected; in-person visit at the branch is mandatory.

entity: Fundación or asociación civil (Código Civil arts. 19-20), registered at the Registro Público (SAREN); subject to the Ley de Fiscalización, Regularización, Actuación y Financiamiento de las ONG y afines (2024).
requirements: Local (Venezuelan) resident officers and registered office, Venezuelan lawyer, notarized deed; 2024 NGO law requires SAREN registration, declaration of foreign funding and donor identification, with dissolution powers; severe exchange and banking restrictions.
cost_time: US$1,000–3,000 incl. lawyer; 3–6+ months (ministerial approval). Notary extra ~US$100–200; official timelines unpublished; bureaucracy heavy.
notes: Major political/economic risk; 2010 Ley de ONGs lets the state restrict entities; foreign funding heavily scrutinized; most international NGOs operate through foreign legal entities, not Venezuelan ones. | Prior context confirmed; 2024/2025 law + donor restrictions make it the hardest in the region; most INGOs use foreign entities | verify-rest 2026-10: no 'Ley Orgánica de Fundaciones' — Civil Code arts. 19-20 govern; 2024 NGO oversight law added; CADIVI (abolished 2014) reference removed
bottleneck: Resident officers + registered office, local lawyer, notarized deed; currency controls; heavy foreign funding scrutiny
deduction: No practical charitable donation deduction regime; NPO tax benefits essentially inoperative
donor_restr: 2024 law (Gaceta 15 Nov 2024): NGOs need state authorization; aimed at restricting international funding; U.S. freeze
compliance: Personality registers with SAREN; no published annual return deadline. Personality is revocable by administrative resolution for statutory breaches; obligations otherwise set by the statutes.
tax_exempt: ISLR art. 14.3: charitable/social-assistance entities whose gains fund their purpose and never distribute profits are exempt — legal, automatic; SENIAT verifies at filing, no separate certificate.
bank_access: Effectively blocked for remote foreigners: banks require cédula de extranjero residency and in-person application; no remote opening; currency controls add friction.

entity: Fundación (1+ founders) or corporación (5+ members) under Decreto Ejecutivo 193/2017 (Reglamento para el Otorgamiento de Personalidad Jurídica a las Organizaciones Sociales), registered in SUIOS via the competent ministry
requirements: Ecuadorian address and legal representative; Ecuadorian lawyer; registration in SUIOS with the competent ministry; ongoing reporting to the supervising ministry.
cost_time: US$500–1,500 incl. lawyer/notary; 2–3 months (Ministerio del Interior). Notary ~US$150–300; official timelines unpublished.
notes: Foreign founders permitted as members/board; Spanish-language documents; IUP status adds time and a public-benefit declaration; banking and tax (SRI) onboarding is slow. | Prior context confirmed; 2025 Social Transparency Organic Law adds registration + foreign-funding controls (30% tax, suspension) | verify-rest 2026-10: Decreto 193/2017 governs; unverifiable 'Ley 2023-13/COEP' removed; ministerial grant carries no government fee
bottleneck: Resident president/board + local address, local lawyer; 2025 social transparency law adds registration & reporting
deduction: Donations deductible up to 5% of net taxable income
donor_restr: 2025 Social Transparency Law: special NGO registry, financial reporting, 30% tax on foreign donations, suspension powers
compliance: Foundations register in the SUIOS/SEPS transparency registry under the 2025 foundations law, filing annual activity and financial reports to the supervisory agency; fines apply for non-compliance.
tax_exempt: Exemption under LRTI art. 9.5 applies to income of private non-profits devoted to their purpose (circular NAC-DGECCGC24-00000006): no separate status; SRI verifies, entity files annual returns. Donors deduct 50%.
bank_access: In-person; most banks want an Ecuadorian cédula, but some (e.g. Banco del Pacífico) accept a passport with a valid visa plus reference under Superintendencia de Bancos rules.

entity: Asociación (Código Civil arts. 80-98), fundación (arts. 99-110) or comité (arts. 111-123) — registro en SUNARP; fundaciones also register with the Consejo de Supervigilancia de Fundaciones (Ministerio de Justicia).
requirements: Public deed registered with SUNARP; local registered office; president/legal rep should be resident in Peru for banking; filings in Spanish.
cost_time: US$300–800 incl. lawyer; 2–6 weeks (notary deed + SUNARP registration). Notary ~US$150–250; official timelines unpublished.
notes: No nationality requirement; foreign founders allowed; tax exemption (exoneración) from SUNAT is separate, discretionary and needs annual reporting; Lima is the practical hub; English not official. | Prior context confirmed; deduction cap is 10% of net taxable income (PwC); SUNAT tax exemption is separate and discretionary | verify-rest 2026-10: Civil Code article numbers corrected; SUNARP fee is modest — the larger figure is notary/lawyer cost
bottleneck: Local registered office + SUNARP public deed; president resident for banking; Spanish filings; separate SUNAT exemption
deduction: Charitable donations deductible up to 10% of net taxable income (PwC)
donor_restr: None notable; foreign funding permitted, no FCRA-style licensing, standard reporting
compliance: Associations and foundations register with Minjus/SUNARP; annual general meeting and statutory compliance are mandatory. No fixed public filing deadline published; persistent breaches can trigger dissolution.
tax_exempt: Separate step: register in the SUNAT “registro de entidades exoneradas del Impuesto a la Renta” (LIR art. 19: educational, scientific, charitable aims). Donors partial deduction; IGV on sales; time unpublished.
bank_access: In-person; full accounts at major banks need a Carné de Extranjería (residency card); a few banks open passport-only savings for non-residents, generally with limits.

entity: Fundación, ONG or entidad civil sin fines de lucro (Ley 351/2013 and DS 1597/2013) — personalidad jurídica from the Ministerio de la Presidencia (multi-department) or departmental Gobernación; cooperativa (Ley 356/2013).
requirements: Resident (Bolivian) officers, local address, notarized deed; foreign-constituted NGOs must sign a framework cooperation agreement with the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Ley 351 art. 13); Spanish only.
cost_time: US$400–1,000 incl. lawyer/notary; 2–4 months. Notary ~US$100–200; official timelines unpublished.
notes: Foreign NGOs must register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería); 2023 law caps foreign government funding for certain activities and tightens oversight; heavy Spanish-language bureaucracy; few English speakers. | verify-rest 2026-10: registering authority corrected (not a 'Superintendencia de Compañías'); unverifiable 'Ley 1417/1475' references removed
bottleneck: Resident officers + local address, notarized deed; foreign-constituted NGOs need a framework agreement with the Foreign Ministry (Ley 351 art. 13)
deduction: Donations to NGOs are tax deductible (Biz Latin Hub)
donor_restr: Foreign-constituted NGOs must sign a framework cooperation agreement with the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Ley 351/2013) and report foreign funding
compliance: Ley 351 (2013) grants and registers personality for foundations and social orgs; the state can dissolve personality by resolution with asset seizure. No published annual return; duties set by internal statutes.
tax_exempt: Not automatic: formalize the IUE (corporate profit) exemption with the SIN (RND 10-0030-05; Ley 843 art. 4) proving charitable purpose and non-distribution. Donor deductions limited (5%/10%); time unpublished.
bank_access: Blocked for non-residents: banks require a Cédula de Identidad de Extranjero and in-person application (ASFI-regulated); tourist status is not enough.

entity: Non-profit company (Companies Act cap. 89:01); friendly society (Friendly Societies Act cap. 36:04); co-operative (Co-operative Societies Act Cap. 88:01 (1948, as am.)).
requirements: Guyanese registered office and resident directors; English is official; no citizenship requirement for board but a local presence is needed; no restrictions on foreign donations.
cost_time: US$300–800 incl. lawyer; 1–3 months at DCRA. Filing ~US$100–300; official timelines unpublished; foreign nationals may incorporate.
notes: Easiest bureaucracy in the sub-region and English-speaking; non-profits face extra scrutiny at formation and take longer than companies; tax exemption is discretionary (Commissioner of Inland Revenue); friendly societies are the most common non-profit form. | Prior context confirmed; English-speaking, easiest bureaucracy in sub-region; tax exemption discretionary; Companies Act 1991
bottleneck: Guyanese registered office + resident directors; English official; no citizenship requirement; no donation restrictions
deduction: Donation deduction available; tax exemption discretionary (Commissioner of Inland Revenue)
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Non-profit companies must file an annual return with the DCRA at least once per year, made up to the AGM date, and keep registered-office records current; failure brings fines, persistent default risks strike-off.
tax_exempt: No general non-profit exemption: the Income Tax Act grants only specific reliefs; the GRA's Tax Exemption, Processing & Verification Division issues individual exemption certificates to qualifying non-profits.
bank_access: In-person visit required with passport, address proof, TIN and source-of-funds disclosure; no statutory ban, but offshore non-resident accounts still need a face-to-face meeting.

entity: Stichting (privaat nut) — Dutch-style foundation by notarial deed under the Stichtingenwet of 19 July 1968; also vereniging (association) and coöperatie.
requirements: Surinamese notary (deeds in Dutch), local board/office in practice; 2013 Dutch-style Civil Code permits stichting with foreign elements but a local notary and presence are required in practice; Dutch language barrier.
cost_time: Official fees unpublished (as of 2026); register fees set by staatsbesluit (Besluit Stichtingenregister G.B. 1970 no. 126, as amended). KKF excerpt SRD 300. Notary ~US$200–500, total ~US$500–1,500; 1–3 months (unofficial estimates).
notes: Dutch is the working language — the main barrier; small legal market; banking requires a local presence; few English-speaking professionals; new Civil Code (in force 2013) modernized foundation law but practice is conservative. | Prior context confirmed; 2013 Civil Code modernized foundation law; notary deed + local presence required in practice | [verified] Stichtingenwet 1968 has no nationality/residence requirement for founder or board, and the seat is the place designated in the articles; but creation requires a notarial deed by a Surinamese notary, so a remote founder needs a notarized power of attorney; banking and practice favor local presence.
bottleneck: Surinamese notary + Dutch deed, local board/office in practice, small legal market, banking requires local presence
deduction: Charitable donation deduction limited; no broad regime; stichting is tax exempt
donor_restr: None notable; foundation law permits foreign elements (ICNL)
compliance: Stichtings are created by notarial deed; no published annual return to the registry. Business activity requires SBN tax registration and annual tax filing. Foundation supervision is by the FIN.
tax_exempt: No automatic charitable exemption: a stichting is taxed as an ordinary legal person (35% income tax on business income); individual exemptions must be requested from the Inland Tax Administration (Dib); VAT applies.
bank_access: No legal residency restriction on foreigners per central-bank guidance; opening is in-person at the bank with passport, address and (often) a foreign bank reference letter.

entity: Associação (Código Civil); fundação (Código Civil); OSCIP (Lei 9.790/1999) — registro em cartório de registro civil de pessoas jurídicas.
requirements: Minimum 2 members (association) or 1 founder (foundation); Brazilian CNPJ and local address; notarial deed registered with a cartório; foreign founder may join the board; filings in Portuguese.
cost_time: US$500–1,500 incl. lawyer/notary; 2–4 months (cartório + optional CGJ certification). Official timelines unpublished; foreigners may set up.
notes: Heavy red tape (famous bureaucracy); main hurdles are getting a CPF and a bank account (foreign-inflow/câmbio rules); OSCIP certification gives donation tax deductions; 'instituição de utilidade pública' (federal/municipal) is a long, discretionary extra step. | Prior context confirmed; deduction is 6% individual / 2% corporate; OSCIP certification required for donor deductions
bottleneck: Local address + CNPJ, cartório deed, resident legal rep for foreign founders, bank account (câmbio rules); Portuguese
deduction: Individuals: up to 6% of IRPF owed (3% child fund + 3% other); corporations: 2% (OSCIP)
donor_restr: OSCIP certification (Ministry of Justice) enables donor tax deductions; ITCMD on foreign donor donations (transitional)
compliance: Associations and foundations register at cartório; no published annual return to the registry. Accounting and tax duties run through a CNPJ with the Receita Federal; internal obligations follow the statutes.
tax_exempt: Income-tax exemption (IRPJ/CSLL/COFINS) for a qualifying non-profit is legal and automatic (Lei 9.532; NFPS) — Receita Federal verifies accounts, no separate recognition. Donor deduction needs utilidade pública/OSCIP.
bank_access: Effectively blocked remotely: banks require CRNM residency, CPF and a Brazilian address with in-person KYC; non-residents are limited to special non-tax-resident (CDE) products.

entity: Asociación civil y fundación (Código Civil, Ley 1183/1985); cooperativa (Ley 438/94) — plus mandatory National Registry of Non-Profit Organizations (MEF) under Ley 7363/2024 and Decreto 4806/2025; Registro Administrativo de Personas y Estructuras Jurídicas (Ley 6446/2019).
requirements: Local registered office and a local representative; notarized deed; founder may be foreign; registration with the relevant ministry/civil registry; Spanish documents.
cost_time: US$300–800 incl. lawyer; 1–3 months (MEF/DGPEJBF). Official timelines unpublished; foreign founders may register with a local representative.
notes: Under-regulated and relatively tolerant of foreign founders, but the legal market is small and Spanish-only; tax exemption requires separate certification; fewer English-speaking lawyers than neighboring countries; slower administration than Chile/Argentina. | Confirm prior; foundation route needs US$400 min. capital in a capital-integration account; NGO route via Min. Interior fee. | verify-rest 2026-10: unverifiable 'Ley 5833/2017' removed; Ley 7363/2024 control/transparency regime added
bottleneck: Local registered office and resident local representative required; Spanish-only documents; small English-capable legal market.
deduction: Donations deductible up to 5% of taxable gross income (renta bruta gravada) to qualifying entities.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Registration in the National Registry of Non-Profit Organizations (MEF) under Ley 7363/2024 and Decreto 4806/2025 with funding/beneficiary reporting; entities receiving state funds must publish accounts to the Contraloría.
tax_exempt: Exemption is legal and automatic: Ley 6.380/19 art. 25.2c exempts income of non-profit associations/foundations that do not distribute (DNIT verifies at filing). Donor deduction limited (5% for individuals).
bank_access: Requires a Paraguayan cédula (residency ID) and in-person presence; a passport alone is not accepted by the major banks, so remote opening is not possible.

entity: Asociación civil or fundación (Ley 17.163/1999) — legal personality recognised by the Ministerio de Educación y Cultura (MEC).
requirements: Minimum 3 persons (association); local registered office; foundation requires a local representative; registration with the Registro Nacional de Personas Jurídicas; Spanish filings.
cost_time: US$200–600 incl. lawyer/notary; 2–6 weeks for MEC recognition. Notary ~US$100–200; official timelines unpublished; foreigners may found.
notes: Very stable, low political risk; foundations enjoy tax incentives (50% exemption on qualifying income); English reasonably available in Montevideo business circles; 'declaración de utilidad pública' optional. | Confirm prior (association from 3 members; foundation needs local rep; foundations enjoy tax incentives). | verify-rest 2026-10: recognition is by the MEC (not the DGR); Ley 17.163 also governs foundations
bottleneck: Local registered office and resident local representative required; filings in Spanish at Registro Nacional de Personas Jurídicas.
deduction: Donations to qualifying associations/foundations get special tax exemptions/incentives under Ley 18.083 (2006).
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Associations and foundations are recognised and supervised by the MEC; foundations file annual accounts with the MEC; no published annual return deadline for associations.
tax_exempt: IRAE exemption of income of qualifying non-profits (educational, cultural, scientific, charitable) is legal and automatic; DGI verifies the purpose. The 75%-refund donor benefit requires listing in the MEF regime.
bank_access: Most open to non-residents: BROU allows a basic in-person account with home-country address, but requires a US$5,000+ fixed deposit held 181 days for new non-residents.

entity: Asociación civil (CCyC arts. 168-192); fundación (CCyC arts. 193-224 y Ley 19.836); fideicomiso (CCyC arts. 1666-1707); cooperativa (Ley 20.337) — registro ante la IGJ (CABA) o la Dirección de Personas Jurídicas provincial.
requirements: Local registered office and resident director/legal rep; foreign founder/trustees allowed; IGJ RG 1/2020 allows constitution without escritura; Spanish filings.
cost_time: US$200–500 incl. lawyer; 2–6 weeks (registro de personas jurídicas; provincial o federal según jurisdicción). Official timelines unpublished.
notes: Most expat-friendly bureaucracy in South America; English widely spoken in Buenos Aires; foreign founders can serve on boards; donation tax exemption is a separate AFIP step ('Ingreso a Régimen de Entidades Exentas', Ley 24.976); 2016 foundation law made fundaciones cheaper and faster than the old regime. | Verified: Sede social en CABA y patrimonio inicial mínimo de 10 salarios mínimos viales y móviles (Res. IGJ 2/2023) | verify-rest 2026-10: legal bases corrected to CCyC + Ley 19.836; registry is IGJ/provincial DPJ, not the commercial registry
bottleneck: Local registered office and resident legal representative; province-by-province association registration plus AFIP steps.
deduction: Donations to qualifying entities deductible up to 5% cap (Ley 24.976, AFIP-exempt entities).
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: IGJ-registered associations and foundations must file approved financial statements annually, fully digital since mid-2026; non-filing brings fines and IGJ regularization windows for arrears.
tax_exempt: Separate certificate required: file DJ 953 with ARCA (ex-AFIP) for “certificado de exención” of Impuesto a las Ganancias (Ley 23.349, reg. 1457) — general or simplified route. Benefits: no income tax, no withholding.
bank_access: In-person at a branch; non-residents can open an account with passport and CUIT/CUIL under BCRA rules; peso savings available even without a DNI, with tighter limits.

entity: Asociación/corporación or fundación (Código Civil Título XXXIII, as amended by Ley 20.500/2011) — Registro Nacional de Personas Jurídicas sin Fines de Lucro (Registro Civil).
requirements: Chilean registered office; board may include foreigners; legal representative should be resident in Chile; constitutive act deposited at the Secretaría Municipal (30-day objection period, CC art. 548); Spanish filings.
cost_time: US$200–500 incl. lawyer; ~1–2 months (municipal 30-day review, then Registro Civil). Foreigners may found with a Chilean representative.
notes: Fast, clean bureaucracy; the de facto hub for LATAM expats and many run foundations/associations there; English widely used in Santiago legal market; donor tax deduction requires 'calificación' from the tax authority; 2015 law modernized foundations. | Verified: Constitución por escritura pública y domicilio en Chile; desde 2023 se inscribe en la Secretaría Municipal | verify-rest 2026-10: 'Ley 20.839' is not the foundations law; filing is at the Secretaría Municipal with a 30-day objection window
bottleneck: Chilean registered office and resident legal representative required; constitutive act deposited at the Secretaría Municipal (30-day review) then Registro Civil.
deduction: Ley 19.885: 35% tax credit + 65% deductible expense for certified qualifying donations.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: OIP organizations must keep the MSGG OIP registry current and file annual activity and financial statements; sanctions include fines. Corporations and foundations file annual accounts to the registry.
tax_exempt: No general entity exemption: fundaciones/corporaciones pay IUS on income. Benefit is for donors: Ley 19.885 gives a 15% credit (individuals) if the entity has ministry-recognized interés público status.
bank_access: In-person; requires a RUT (foreigners with a valid visa can get a provisional one) and ID per ChileAtiende rules; non-residents without RUT/visa are effectively blocked.

entity: Private foundation (хувийн сан); Association (нийгмийн эвлэл); NGO under the Law on Associations (1997) + Civil Code (2002)
requirements: As a Mongolian citizen you register with the Legal Entity Registration Office (LERO, Justice ministry) with a Mongolian-language notarized charter, a local registered address, and a governing board (minimum 5 members for non-membership NGOs); a foundation requires an endowment adequate to its stated purpose.
cost_time: Modest state fees (tens of USD) plus notarization; typically 2–8 weeks for registration.
notes: Scored on the local-citizen route, which is straightforward — no foreign-founder bar. bank_access: A registered Albanian firm can open a corporate account, but non-resident owners face enhanced AML due diligence; banks (Raiffeisen, BKT) will process it, and a signatory branch visit is the norm.

entity: Public associations (2+ founders); foundations; registered by the Public Services Agency under Law 86/2020 on Non-commercial Organisations. Foreigners may found with local involvement.
requirements: Association 2+ founders (natural or legal persons; foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language charter (Russian widely used in practice); foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
cost_time: No state registration fee (2020 NCO law); about EUR 100-300 for notary and legal support only. Processing 2-6 weeks; no official processing time published.
notes: Cheap; EU candidate; political/economic volatility and weak enforcement; banking for foreign directors can be fiddly. | Confirm association/foundation and 2-6 weeks; no state registration fee (Lex Mundi guide), prior 100-300 EUR was notary/legal only. | verify-rest 2026-10: Law 86/2020 allows 2 founders; registration free with a 15-day statutory term

donor_restr: None notable; no foreign-agent or foreign-funded-NGO registration regime.
compliance: NCO Law (86/2020): annual activity report published within 6 months of year-end; no formal strike-off for late filing, but activity contrary to national security or public order grounds termination.
tax_exempt: Automatic: Law 86/2020 associations and foundations are income-tax exempt once they perform socially useful activities within 1 year (Tax Code). Donor deduction rate unpublished. Time unpublished.
bank_access: In-person signing at a Chisinau branch is standard; non-resident UBOs trigger enhanced due diligence under AML Law 30/2011 and banks demand detailed source-of-funds documentation.

entity: Hromadska orhanizatsiia (public association, Law 4572-VI); blahodiinyi fond (charitable foundation, Law 5073-VI on Charitable Activities and Charitable Organizations); non-profit status via the tax register
requirements: Organization 2+ founders (foreign individuals must be lawfully staying in Ukraine), local office, Ukrainian-language documents; online registration.
cost_time: State registration of a public association is free; translations/notary extra; statutory review ~3 working days, ~1-2 weeks total
notes: Registration itself is cheap and fast, but active war, banking/sanctions friction for a foreign resident founder and currency risk make this a risky base; many Western expat charities run via local Ukrainian partners. | verify-rest 2026-10: no state duty for public-association registration; 'fundatsiia' replaced with blahodiinyi fond
bottleneck: War risk, banking/sanctions friction; Ukrainian-language documents + certified translations required.
deduction: Donations deductible, capped at 3% of annual total income.
donor_restr: Ukrainian orgs with foreign-state funding >20% of total must register as foreign-agent organizations (2015 law).
compliance: The annual activity-report duty under the Public Organisations Law (4572-VI) was abolished (Law 767-VII); no periodic registrar filing for typical NGOs, only standard legal-entity tax and financial reporting.
tax_exempt: Automatic on state registration (Tax Code art.132); 'public benefit' status is separate. Donor deductions: corporate 2-5% of prior profit, individual 1%; some services VAT-exempt. Time unpublished.
bank_access: NBU rules allow banks to serve non-residents and foreign-owned Ukrainian entities open accounts routinely, but expect full KYC/AML, apostilled documents, and usually an in-person visit or notarized power of attorney.

entity: publicnaya organizatsiya (public organization), fundatsiya (foundation)
requirements: Public association needs 10+ founders (local) or 50+ (republican) under the Law on Public Associations (1994, as amended 2023); local office; Russian- or Belarusian-language charter; foreign-funded NGOs face heavy restrictions.
cost_time: Nominally low fees, 1-3 months; in practice effectively barred for an independent foreign founder
notes: 2021+ crackdown on independent civil society; heavy political risk; private foundations rare and state-dominated; not recommended for this founder. | Confirm effectively barred: ICNL notes foreign citizens cannot be founders of public associations; spring96: KGB approval from 2027. | verify-rest 2026-10: founder minimum is 10 (local) / 50 (republican)
bottleneck: Foreigners barred from founding associations; KGB security checks for new NGOs from 2027; heavy political risk.
deduction: No meaningful individual charitable-donation deduction regime.
donor_restr: Since 2021, foreign-funded NGOs risk 'undesirable organization' designation and ban; security vetting of founders.
compliance: Each year by 1 March the association sends the registering authority its continued-activity information and the list of elected governing-body members; foundations also publish an annual property report.
tax_exempt: Public organizations and foundations are non-taxable on donations, budget funds and membership fees under the Tax Code - no separate application. Donor deduction rate unpublished. Time unpublished.
bank_access: Currency law permits non-residents to hold BYN and foreign-currency accounts, but certified documents, UBO disclosure and bank AML/KYC apply; expect an in-person visit (or authorized representative) in Minsk.

entity: asociație (association), fundație (foundation)
requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language statute; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
cost_time: ~500 RON state fee + notary ~1,000-2,000 RON; ~1-3 months (statutory 30 days)
notes: EU member; moderate bureaucracy; 'de utilitate publică' (public-benefit) tax status is a separate, stricter procedure; English support OK in Bucharest/Cluj. | Confirm association/foundation and separate public-utility status; state fee ~300 RON (~$70), prior 500 RON overstated.
bottleneck: Notarized founding deed + local office; 'de utilitate publica' status needs a separate court procedure.
deduction: Donations to public-utility organizations deductible, capped at 10% of annual income.
donor_restr: None notable (EU); no foreign-agent-style registration regime.
compliance: Ordinance 26/2000: annual activity and financial reports to the competent administrative authority, published in the Official Gazette; late filing risks fines or deregistration.
tax_exempt: Non-commercial income is exempt from income tax automatically; 'public benefit' status is a separate Ministry of Justice application. Donor deductions: individual 10% of income, corporate 10% of profit.
bank_access: An in-person branch visit by the company administrator is generally required; AML rules impose enhanced due diligence on non-resident directors, and fully remote opening at high-street banks is largely unavailable.

entity: Non-profit legal entities (NPL) under the Non-Profit Legal Entities Act; associations; foundations; registered at the Agency for Registration. A 1-founder NPL is the simplest route.
requirements: Foundation needs only 1 founder; association needs 3+ founders (7 natural or 3 legal persons for public-benefit) (NPLE Act Art. 19); foreigners allowed; local office; Bulgarian-language documents.
cost_time: Registry Agency fee ~EUR 25 (euro since 1 Jan 2026) plus notary fees; statutory 30 days. Foreigners can found an NPLE; no residency requirement for the founding act itself.
notes: EU member; the 1-founder NPL form is the simplest for a lone foreign founder; good English support in Sofia; cheap to operate. | Confirm 1-founder NPL as simplest route; fees ~150-300 BGN plus notary; 30-day statutory limit as prior. | verify-rest 2026-10: association founder minimum is 3; Registry Agency fee ~EUR 25
bottleneck: Local office + notarized deed; Bulgarian-language documents; foreign founder acts via notarized power of attorney.
deduction: Donations to public-benefit organizations deductible, capped at 10% of annual income.
donor_restr: None notable (EU); no foreign-agent-style registration regime.
compliance: Triple annual filing: activity report to Statistics (due ~31 May), financial statements to the NRA if income or expenses exceed 500 BGN, and an annual fee to the registration office; neglect risks deregistration.
tax_exempt: PBO status needs separate Central Register entry (Ministry of Justice) - PBOs exempt from CIT when income serves public benefit. Donor deductions: individual 5% of income, corporate 10% of profit.
bank_access: Banks require in-person verification: personal accounts always, and corporate accounts usually need the director to appear; a non-resident founder should plan a visit or appoint a local agent to sign.

entity: Associations (somateio, min. 20 founders, Civil Code art. 78); foundations (Civil Code arts. 108-121 + Law 5259/2025, which repealed Law 4182/2013); general-benefit status via separate application.
requirements: Association needs 20+ founders (foreigners allowed), Greek registered office, Greek-language charter registered by order of the Magistrates' Court (Eirinodikeio); foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
cost_time: About EUR 500-1500 in notary and legal fees; 1-3 months. Foreigners may be founders; general-benefit status is a separate, discretionary step.
notes: Paper/notary-heavy process, Greek language required, no meaningful online registry; foundations now under Law 5259/2025; use a local lawyer. | verify-rest 2026-10: somateio needs 20 founders; registration via Magistrates' Court since 2016; Law 5259/2025 replaced 4182/2013
bottleneck: Greek-language notary deed + court registry filing + Greek registered office; local lawyer/notary needed remotely
time_to_reg: 2-4 months (notary + Magistrates' Court registration; slower for remote founders)
deduction: Up to 10% of taxable income for donations to approved public-benefit orgs
donor_restr: None notable; no FCRA-style foreign-donor restriction on EU or overseas donations to public-benefit orgs
compliance: Foundations (Law 4182/2013, art. 59) submit budget, final accounts and balance sheet to the competent authority yearly and an asset-usage plan every two years; non-compliance risks deregistration.
tax_exempt: General public-benefit status: separate application to the Directorate for Associations (Law 4873/2021); recognized bodies exempt from tax on contributions. Donor cut: 20% of gifts over EUR 100, cap 10% of income.
bank_access: A Greek tax number (AFM) is a hard precondition, and branches require an in-person visit with due diligence on the account's purpose; there is no fully online route for non-residents.

entity: Charitable trust (unregistered); society (20+ founders) or institution (idryma, 1 founder) under the Societies and Institutions Law 104(I)/2017; company limited by guarantee with a Council of Ministers licence (Companies Law Cap. 113, s.20)
requirements: A charitable trust needs only a settlor + trustee and no registration; a society needs 20+ founding persons and an institution 1 founder, plus a local address, registered with the District Officer/Registrar; English fully accepted.
cost_time: Trust: ~500-2,000 EUR via solicitor, days; society/institution: ~100-500 EUR, up to ~3 months (Registrar review)
notes: English common-law jurisdiction — most expats set up a simple charitable trust with a Cypriot trustee; tax deductibility requires income-tax authority approval and a Cypriot public-benefit nexus; strong English-language professional services. | verify-rest 2026-10: society needs 20 founders under Law 104(I)/2017; Registrar may take up to 3 months
bottleneck: Trust unregistered (easiest); registered body needs Cypriot head office + 7 members + local agent for bank account
time_to_reg: days-weeks (trust via solicitor); up to ~3 months (society/institution — Registrar has 3 months to examine)
deduction: Donations to qualifying orgs deductible up to 30% of taxable income; 5% of excess over EUR 150,000
donor_restr: None notable; no FCRA-style regime; deductibility tracks the org's TRA approval, not donor nationality
compliance: Societies notify the registrar annually on administrative matters; non-profit companies file annual returns and accounts within ~9-12 months of year-end, with late-filing penalties and deregistration risk.
tax_exempt: Separate approval by the Tax Dept/MOF; approved charities get preferential treatment and donors deduct 100% of gifts from taxable income, no cap (ITL 118(I)/2002 art.9). Time unpublished.
bank_access: Residency is not a legal bar, but local banks require in-person KYC and source-of-funds checks under Central Bank of Cyprus AML rules; non-residents are often flagged high-risk. EMIs (Wise, Revolut) open online.

entity: association (Voluntary Organisations Act (Ch. 492, 2007)), foundation, charitable trust
requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local registered address; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed; English fully accepted.
cost_time: Association ~150-500 EUR, ~days-2 weeks (online); foundation ~1,500-5,000 EUR, ~2-6 weeks
notes: English official language, streamlined 2021 framework; foundation is the stronger form for asset-holding; charitable trusts available under trust law without registration. | Association min 3 members + 3 administrators under Act V/2021; MBR online filing, English accepted. Confirm prior fees/timeline.
bottleneck: Malta registered office + at least 3 administrators required; local address provider solves remote bottleneck
deduction: Up to 30% of taxable income for donations to public-benefit orgs
donor_restr: None notable; no FCRA-style foreign-donor restriction; public-benefit status is the key test
compliance: Enrolled VOs submit Annual Returns (return, report, accounts) to the Commissioner for Voluntary Organisations after each financial year (S.L. 492.02); the register is public; non-compliance risks deregistration.
tax_exempt: Not automatic: apply to Revenue & Customs Administration for income-tax exemption for philanthropic work (LN 62/2024). Corporate donors get tax credit on qualifying gifts (cap EUR 500, LN 86/2024). Time unpublished.
bank_access: Traditional banks (BOV, HSBC Malta, APS Bank) require at least one in-person branch visit; fully remote opening is generally unavailable from abroad, with 2-6 weeks to account activation.

entity: Companies limited by guarantee (most charities); incorporated associations; registered with the CRO and then with the Charities Regulator (Charities Act 2009).
requirements: Irish registered office and at least one EEA-resident director (or a EUR 25,000 s.137 bond / s.140 certificate); every charity operating in Ireland must register with the Charities Regulator regardless of income
cost_time: CRO incorporation about EUR 100; Charities Regulator registration is free; 4-8 weeks. Foreign directors permitted if the EEA-residency rule or bond is met.
notes: English-language, common-law system; no nationality requirement for trustees; most overseas founders set up a company limited by guarantee with a local registered-office agent, then register the charity | Confirm prior; regulator is the Charities Regulatory Authority (CRA), not the former 'Charity Commission for Ireland'. | verify-rest 2026-10: no EUR 50k registration threshold; regulator is the Charities Regulator; s.137 requires an EEA-resident director or bond
bottleneck: Irish registered office + management and control in Ireland; a local registered-office agent is typical.
deduction: Tax-deductible at donor's marginal rate; 25% tax credit for corporate donors.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Charities Act 2009 s.52: Annual Report to the Charities Regulator within 10 months of year-end (31 October for December year-end); non-filing is an offence and the Regulator may strike the charity off.
tax_exempt: Two-step: register with the Charities Regulator first, then apply to Revenue for charitable tax exemption (CHY number) - exempts income tax, CIT, CGT, DIRT; donors get 25%/33.33% tax credits. Time unpublished.
bank_access: Irish banks expect local substance — typically a resident (Irish/EEA) director and an Irish operational base; boards with only non-resident, no-presence directors are frequently declined at onboarding.

entity: Registered charity (Charity Commission England & Wales), company limited by guarantee, charitable trust
requirements: Charity must be established and administered in the UK (UK address, UK-law governing document); no trustee residency or citizenship requirement; Charity Commission registration required above GBP 5,000 income (CIOs register at any income)
cost_time: CLG at Companies House £100 (was £12; fee change effective 1 Feb 2026, announced 30 Oct 2025); Charity Commission registration free; ~8–12 weeks (Charity Commission 2025-26: median ~12 weeks to full registration)
notes: English-language, common law; the most popular expat-charity pathway; overseas individuals may be trustees provided management and control are in the UK | Verified: Must be based in England/Wales (local postal address + governing document); no trustee-residency rule. | Verified 2026: Charities Act 2011 as amended by Charities Act 2022 (commencement regs in force from 2025). | verify-rest 2026-10: no UK-resident trustee requirement; registration threshold GBP 5,000 (CIOs always register)
bottleneck: Charity must be established and managed in the UK: UK address and UK-based trustees/management in practice.
deduction: Gift Aid: UK taxpayers reclaim basic-rate tax on gifts to registered charities.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Charities Act 2011: annual return and accounts to the Charity Commission within 10 months of the accounting reference date; accounts are public; persistent non-filing risks removal from the register.
tax_exempt: Charity Commission registration (charitable purposes, public benefit; mandatory above GBP 5,000): exempts income/corporate tax, Gift Aid 25% donor gross-up, VAT exemption for qualifying supplies. Target 30 working days.
bank_access: Non-residents can open UK business accounts, but AML/KYC and sanctions checks apply; high-street banks often expect a UK address and evidence of genuine UK activity — possible, though tighter than for residents.

entity: Associations / third-sector organisations (Act 110/2021); non-business foundations (sjálfseignarstofnanir, Act 19/1988 as am. by Act 112/2024; charter approved by the District Commissioner) or business foundations (Act 33/1999); tax-deductible status via Skatturinn's public-benefit register (almannaheillaskrá).
requirements: Icelandic registered address and local contact; association needs ~5 members; foundation requires ~ISK 3m endowment and Icelandic management
cost_time: Association registration about ISK 5,000-10,000; 2-4 weeks. Foundations require a minimum endowment of about ISK 1,000,000; foreigners may found.
notes: Documents in Icelandic; tax-deductible status requires registration on Skatturinn's public-benefit register; small bureaucracy but limited English support | verify-rest 2026-10: charitable foundations fall under Act 19/1988 (Act 33/1999 is for business foundations); third-sector Act 110/2021; RSK is now Skatturinn
bottleneck: Icelandic registered address, Icelandic-language documents, ~5 members; tax exemption is a separate application.
deduction: Deductible if the organisation is on Skatturinn's public-benefit register (almannaheillaskrá); individuals deduct ISK 10,000-350,000/yr, companies up to 1.5% of income.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Plain associations have no statutory annual filing to the register; entities within the Act on Annual Accounts file accounts by 31 August; the general meeting adopts the annual report and accounts.
tax_exempt: General exemption from income and property tax, no separate application. Donors deduct ISK 10,000-350,000/yr for gifts to bodies on the public-benefit register; fundraising activities VAT-exempt.
bank_access: Banks require an Icelandic kennitala (national ID) and in-person ID verification; company law also expects at least half the board to be resident, so a local presence or representative is effectively needed.

entity: Member associations (lag, unregulated — 2020-21 draft never enacted; simple Brønnøysund registration); foundations; both registered with the Brønnøysund Register. No minimum capital; a simple notification regime.
requirements: Norwegian address for the association (min. 2 founders, no nationality rules); foundation needs NOK 100,000 capital (NOK 200,000 commercial) and incurs a registration fee (~NOK 2,656 online)
cost_time: Association registration at Brønnøysund is FREE; 2-6 weeks. Foreigners may be members and board; no local residency required for registration.
notes: Online via Altinn with English available; association is simple but requires a local contact; foundations have strict Norwegian-control rules | Prior cost corrected: initial association registration at Brønnøysund is free (not NOK 1,000-2,500). | verify-rest 2026-10: association needs 2 founders; foundation minimum capital NOK 100,000
bottleneck: Norwegian address and resident board contact; registration is online via Altinn (English available).
deduction: Deductible via gavefradrag, capped at NOK 30,000/yr, if the organisation qualifies.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Foundations file annual report and accounts with the Register of Company Accounts by 31 July; plain associations only if they have an accounting obligation; late filing incurs fees and supervision.
tax_exempt: Automatic income and wealth tax exemption when non-commercial (no profit to members). Donors deduct up to NOK 25,000 (2026) for monetary gifts of NOK 500+ to approved organizations. Time unpublished.
bank_access: Registered entities can open accounts, but banks demand board-member ID verification and proof of Norwegian business activity under AML rules; non-resident directors should be EEA-resident and expect a branch visit.

entity: Associations (yhdistys, 3+ founders, Associations Act 503/1989); foundations (säätiö, Foundations Act 487/2015, EUR 50,000 minimum capital); registered with PRH. Charitable status via the Tax Administration.
requirements: Finnish address; association needs 3+ founding members; foundation needs EUR 50,000 minimum basic capital (PRH fee ~EUR 920) and an EEA-resident board
cost_time: PRH registration fee about EUR 100; 1-3 months. Foreigners may be members; no residency requirement to found an association.
notes: Finnish-language requirement for documents and minutes; PRH bureaucracy is the main burden; foundations are hard for a foreign founder | confirm prior; PRH registration fee is about EUR 100. | verify-rest 2026-10: association needs 3 founders; foundation minimum capital EUR 50,000
bottleneck: Finnish registered address + local service recipient; Finnish/Swedish-language statutes; PRH processing slow.
deduction: Deductible if the association holds a gift-deduction (lahjoitusvähennys) certificate.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Most associations have no annual filing duty; larger ones (two of: assets EUR 7.5m, turnover EUR 15m, 50 employees) file financial statements with the PRH Register of Associations; non-filing risks fines.
tax_exempt: Donation deduction: the organization must be on the Tax Administration's approved-donation list (separate application). Monetary gifts to approved orgs are deductible. Time unpublished.
bank_access: Banks treat non-EEA directors/UBOs as high-risk; identification at a branch (or strong eID) is required, and non-residents without a Finnish HETU code often face long, complex reviews ending in generic refusal.

entity: Ideell förening (non-profit association; organisation number from Skatteverket, form SKV 8400, free); ekonomisk förening (registered at Bolagsverket); stiftelse (foundation, county administrative board).
requirements: Swedish registered seat (säte) and min. 3 members for the association, no residency requirement; foundation needs ~SEK 250k+ and a Swedish-resident board
cost_time: About SEK 1,000-2,500; 4-8 weeks. A bank account needs a D-number. Foreigners may be members; no residency rule for founding.
notes: Straightforward online registration with Bolagsverket, English widely understood; a Swedish bank account for the entity typically requires a personal/D-number for the signatory | verify-rest 2026-10: ideell förening gets its org. number from Skatteverket free; Bolagsverket fee applies only to economic associations
bottleneck: Swedish registered seat (säte) required; board residency not required; Bolagsverket online registration.
fee_usd: $0 for an ideell förening (Skatteverket); ~$180-210 for an ekonomisk förening (SEK 1,900 online)
deduction: Deductible if the association qualifies as tax-exempt (skattefri) under the tax-exemption rules.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Foundations file annual reports with Bolagsverket within 7.5 months of year-end (late-filing fees); simple associations have no statutory filing duty, accounts are adopted at the general meeting.
tax_exempt: Dues, donations and grants tax-exempt; other income exempt if 4 public-benefit conditions met. Donor relief (25% tax cut, cap SEK 3,000) needs separate Skatteverket application as gift recipient.
bank_access: Foreign-owned companies can open accounts, but traditional banks apply strict residency-based KYC; at least 50% of the board must be EEA-resident (waivable by Bolagsverket) and a branch visit is standard.

entity: Voluntary associations (frivillige foreninger); foundations; associations registered with the CVR register. The Act on Foundations and Certain Associations (LBK nr. 2020 of 11/12/2020, as amended) applies to foundations.
requirements: Danish address, min. 2 members, registered in the CVR register; Foundations Act (LBK 2020/2020) requires a Danish-resident board majority for foundations
cost_time: Association registration at CVR is free; DKK 0-2,000 total with legal support; 2-6 weeks. Foundations Act (LBK 2020/2020) requires a Danish-resident board majority.
notes: Association name and documents must be in Danish; CVR registration itself is easy; Danish-controlled foundation rules make the foundation route hard for a foreigner | verify-rest 2026-10: LB 938/2012 superseded by consolidated LBK nr. 2020 of 11/12/2020

deduction: 30A scheme: donor's gift is tax-deductible; 19% of the gift (income tax) goes to the state.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Voluntary associations (frivillige foreninger) have no statutory reporting duty to CVR, only re-confirmation of the CVR number every 3 years; annual accounts are prepared for members; inactivity risks deregistration.
tax_exempt: Non-commercial association income exempt automatically on CVR registration. Donor deduction: up to DKK 20,000/yr (2026) for gifts to tax-approved orgs under Tax Act s.8A. Time unpublished.
bank_access: Danish substance — local clients, office or employees — is effectively required; banks demand MitID and strict AML/KYC on foreign owners, so all-non-resident files are often refused; fintech accounts are easier.

entity: Non-profit association (MTÜ), nonprofit foundation (sihtasutus)
requirements: Estonian registered address (virtual office available); MTÜ needs 2+ members, no nationality rules; sihtasutus has no statutory minimum endowment (management + supervisory board required)
cost_time: State fee EUR 30 (MTÜ) / EUR 80 + notary ~40-50 (sihtasutus); 1-3 business days (MTÜ); 5 business days (sihtasutus)
notes: 100% online e-Business Register with English available; no local-national requirement; among the easiest jurisdictions for a foreign founder | verified primary: official state-fee table 01.01.2022 (abiinfo.rik.ee): non-profit association 30 EUR, foundation 80 EUR; MTÜ min. 2 members (Non-profit Associations Act, unified form since 2016); e-Residency online filing possible | Verified: Estonian ID-card/e-Residency ID needed for online signing; foreign founders allowed

deduction: Deductible for individuals up to 300% of statutory minimum wage (2026 cap ~EUR 3,780), indexed annually; no foreign-donor restrictions.
donor_restr: none notable
compliance: Non-profit associations (MTU) submit annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement) to the e-Business Register within 6 months of year-end (30 June for calendar year); non-filing risks removal.
tax_exempt: Registration automatic; separate EMTA list application required (Income Tax Act s.11) - listed orgs: donation income not taxable. Donors: individuals up to EUR 1,200; corporate 3% social tax base or 10% prior profit.
bank_access: An Estonian bank account is not legally required — EEA EMIs (Wise, LHV online) serve non-resident companies — but Estonian banks approve such files mostly with real local operation or a local board member.

entity: Associations (biedrības) and foundations (nodibinājumi) under the Associations and Foundations Law (adopted 30 Oct 2003, in force 1 Apr 2004), registered in the Enterprise Register via the e-portal.
requirements: Latvian address and Latvian-language name/documents; e-filing via registrs.ur.gov.lv with a Latvian/EU e-signature needs no notary (paper filings need notarised signatures)
cost_time: State fee EUR 11.38 (10% less online); total EUR 30-100; 1-4 weeks. E-filing with an e-signature avoids the notary step. A Latvian address is required.

Real barriers: Latvian-resident board requirement plus local address and e-ID | verify-rest 2026-10: law date corrected to 2003/2004; no '2016 Nonprofit Organizations Law' exists; state fee EUR 11.38 (Cabinet Reg. 308)

deduction: Donations to public-benefit organizations (PBOs) deductible from personal income, within statutory caps

tax_exempt: Registration automatic; PBO status is a separate VID application (Public Benefit Organisation Law) - PBOs exempt from income tax. Donors: individuals 25.5% tax refund; corporate 5% of prior profit or CIT reduction.
bank_access: Since the 2018 reforms, business accounts for non-resident owners are hard to approve (2-4 weeks, elevated refusals); banks require proof of a Latvia connection and usually a visit; EU/EEA applicants can apply remotely.

entity: Association (asociacija, Law on Associations), public institution (viešoji įstaiga), charity and support foundation (labdaros ir paramos fondas)
requirements: Lithuanian address, Lithuanian-language name and documents; board and min. 1–2 founders depending on form; registration via e-signature or notary with the Register of Legal Entities
cost_time: State fee ~€20–50 (plus notary if offline); ~3–10 business days
notes: The fully online route requires a Lithuanian e-ID, so a foreign founder usually acts through a local notary or representative; otherwise the process is fast | confirm prior: state fee ~€25.65, registry completes in ~7 working days; online route needs Lithuanian e-signature, so a local notary/agent is usual | verify-rest 2026-10: 'NVO' is not a legal form — forms corrected
bottleneck: Lithuanian address, Lithuanian-language documents, and a Lithuanian e-signature for online filing — a local notary is typical
deduction: Donations to public-benefit orgs deductible: individuals 10% cap; corporates 2x up to 40% of profit
donor_restr: none notable — no FCRA-style foreign-donor registration; public-benefit (VLO) status is an optional separate registration
